text:
`python3 -m unittest` now passes all 25 tests. I didn't touch any test files. There were six root-cause bugs:

- **`queue.py`:** `_Entry.sort_key` ordered by `(seq, -priority)`. It now orders by `(-priority, seq)`, so higher priority goes first and ties are FIFO.
- **`retry.py`:** `should_retry` had an off-by-one, `attempts_made < max_attempts - 1`. It is now `attempts_made < max_attempts`.
- **`events.py`:** `_prefix_matches` had its arguments reversed, using `prefix.startswith(topic + ".")`. It now uses `topic.startswith(prefix + ".")`.
- **`statemachine.py`:** `batch_order_ok` required priorities to be non-decreasing within an admission batch. It now requires non-increasing. The wrong check made the scheduler fail any lower-priority task admitted after a higher one.
- **`resources.py`:** `ResourcePool.release` subtracted 1 instead of `cost`, which leaked capacity and stalled any task that needed more than one unit.
- **`config.py`:** `deep_merge` recursed with its arguments swapped, so the defaults overrode a task's own nested settings such as `retry.max_attempts`.

I also changed `scheduler.py`. `_cascade_skip` used `dag.dependents`, which returns only direct children, so a failure skipped just the next layer. It now uses `dag.transitive_dependents` to skip everything downstream.
